title: God’s Promises — Comprehensive Searchable Catalog
translationNote: Scripture quotations are from the World English Bible (public domain). Paraphrase fields are original plain-language summaries for searchability, not additional Bible text. Entries prioritize clear divine promissory statements and closely related sworn assurances attributed as God’s word.
expandHint: Continue deepening thinner books (Historicals narrative, minor prophets judgment oracles, Mark, some wisdom). Prefer distinct promise units over padding every adjacent verse.

coverageNotes.methodology: Inclusion favors God speaking commitment, covenant, assurance, or sworn word; also NT apostolic declarations of God’s sure commitment in Christ. Ministries that claim '~3000 promises' often count every blessing, command-with-benefit, or inferred assurance differently—this catalog is curated for pastoral search quality, not maximum count.

promises.promise: God blesses people and gives them a good place in his world—to grow, care for creation, and live under his kindness.
promises.text: God blessed them. God said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth, and subdue it. Have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the sky, and over every living thing that moves on the earth.”
promises.context: Spoken at creation, after God made people in his image.

promises.promise: God promises to provide what people need. He gives plants and fruit from the earth as food.
promises.text: God said, “Behold, I have given you every herb yielding seed, which is on the surface of all the earth, and every tree, which bears fruit yielding seed. It will be your food.
promises.context: God’s kind provision in the world he made.

promises.promise: God promises that evil will not win forever. One day the woman’s child will crush the serpent’s head—even though it will cost him pain.
promises.text: I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.”
promises.context: God’s words to the serpent after the fall in Eden.

promises.promise: God promises he will never again curse the ground as he did, or destroy every living thing the way he did in the flood.
promises.text: The LORD smelled the pleasant aroma. The LORD said in his heart, “I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake because the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth. I will never again strike every living thing, as I have done.
promises.context: After the flood, when Noah offered worship to God.

promises.promise: God promises that as long as the earth remains, seasons, day, and night will keep going. You can trust the steady rhythms he made.
promises.text: While the earth remains, seed time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night will not cease.”
promises.context: God’s quiet decision after the flood to keep the world stable for life.

promises.promise: After the flood, God again blesses people to be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth.
promises.text: God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, and replenish the earth.
promises.context: God’s first words to Noah’s family after they leave the ark.

promises.promise: God makes a lasting promise to Noah, his family, and every living creature: never again will a flood wipe out all life on the earth.
promises.text: “As for me, behold, I establish my covenant with you, and with your offspring after you, and with every living creature that is with you: the birds, the livestock, and every animal of the earth with you, of all that go out of the ship, even every animal of the earth. I will establish my covenant with you: All flesh will not be cut off any more by the waters of the flood. There will never again be a flood to destroy the earth.”
promises.context: God speaks to Noah and his sons after the flood.

promises.promise: God gives the rainbow as a sign of his promise. When he sees it, he remembers his word—never again will a flood destroy all life.
promises.text: God said, “This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations: I set my rainbow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth. When I bring a cloud over the earth, that the rainbow will be seen in the cloud, I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh, and the waters will no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. The rainbow will be in the cloud. I will look at it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth.”
promises.context: God gives Noah a visible token of the flood lasting promise.

promises.promise: God promises to bless Abram, make him into a great people, and bring blessing to all families on earth through him.
promises.text: I will make of you a great nation. I will bless you and make your name great. You will be a blessing. I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse him who treats you with contempt. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you.”
promises.context: God calls Abram to leave home for a land God will show him.

promises.promise: God promises to give the land of Canaan to Abram’s children.
promises.text: The LORD appeared to Abram and said, “I will give this land to your offspring.” He built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
promises.context: At Shechem, after Abram entered Canaan.

promises.promise: God gives Abram all the land he can see, forever, and children as countless as the dust of the earth.
promises.text: The LORD said to Abram, after Lot was separated from him, “Now, lift up your eyes, and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward, for I will give all the land which you see to you and to your offspring forever. I will make your offspring as the dust of the earth, so that if a man can count the dust of the earth, then your offspring may also be counted. Arise, walk through the land in its length and in its width; for I will give it to you.”
promises.context: After Abram and Lot parted ways over grazing land.

promises.promise: God tells Abram not to be afraid. He himself will be Abram’s shield and his very great reward.
promises.text: After these things the LORD’s word came to Abram in a vision, saying, “Don’t be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your exceedingly great reward.”
promises.context: After Abram rescued Lot and refused the king of Sodom’s spoils.

promises.promise: Abram’s heir will be his own child, and his children will be as countless as the stars.
promises.text: Behold, the LORD’s word came to him, saying, “This man will not be your heir, but he who will come out of your own body will be your heir.” The LORD brought him outside, and said, “Look now toward the sky, and count the stars, if you are able to count them.” He said to Abram, “So your offspring will be.”
promises.context: Abram had feared a household servant would be his heir.

promises.promise: God tells ahead of time about oppression in a foreign land, then promises judgment on that nation and deliverance with great wealth.
promises.text: He said to Abram, “Know for sure that your offspring will live as foreigners in a land that is not theirs, and will serve them. They will afflict them four hundred years. I will also judge that nation, whom they will serve. Afterward they will come out with great wealth;
promises.context: During the lasting promise ceremony when Abram asked how he would know he would inherit the land.

promises.promise: God promises to give Abram’s children the land from Egypt’s river to the Euphrates.
promises.text: In that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, “I have given this land to your offspring, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates:
promises.context: Sealed by God alone passing between the lasting promise pieces.

promises.promise: God’s angel promises lonely Hagar that her children will become too many to count. She is not forgotten.
promises.text: The LORD’s angel said to her, “I will greatly multiply your offspring, that they will not be counted for multitude.”
promises.context: Hagar fled from Sarai and met the angel of the Lord by a spring in the wilderness.

promises.promise: God gives a new name to Abram as Abraham, father of many nations, and pledges an everlasting lasting promise: to be their God and give Canaan as an everlasting possession.
promises.text: “As for me, behold, my covenant is with you. You will be the father of a multitude of nations. Your name will no more be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham; for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations. I will make you exceedingly fruitful, and I will make nations of you. Kings will come out of you. I will establish my covenant between me and you and your offspring after you throughout their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God to you and to your offspring after you. I will give to you, and to your offspring after you, the land where you are traveling, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession. I will be their God.”
promises.context: When Abraham was ninety-nine years old, God appeared as God Almighty.

promises.promise: God gives a new name to Sarai as Sarah and promises her a son; she will be a mother of nations and kings.
promises.text: God said to Abraham, “As for Sarai your wife, you shall not call her name Sarai, but her name shall be Sarah. I will bless her, and moreover I will give you a son by her. Yes, I will bless her, and she will be a mother of nations. Kings of peoples will come from her.”
promises.context: Part of the same lasting promise appearance when Abraham was ninety-nine.

promises.promise: Sarah will bear Isaac, and God will establish an everlasting lasting promise with him and his children.
promises.text: God said, “No, but Sarah, your wife, will bear you a son. You shall call his name Isaac. I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant for his offspring after him.
promises.context: Abraham had asked that Ishmael might live before God.

promises.promise: God has heard Abraham’s prayer for Ishmael. He will bless him, multiply him, and make him a great nation.
promises.text: As for Ishmael, I have heard you. Behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly. He will become the father of twelve princes, and I will make him a great nation.
promises.context: God answers Abraham’s plea for Ishmael while confirming the lasting promise line through Isaac.

promises.promise: God promises Sarah will have a son—within a year, just as he said.
promises.text: He said, “I will certainly return to you at about this time next year; and behold, Sarah your wife will have a son.” Sarah heard in the tent door, which was behind him.
promises.context: Three visitors appear to Abraham by the oaks of Mamre; Sarah listens from the tent.

promises.promise: Nothing is too hard for the Lord; he will return at the appointed time and Sarah will have a son.
promises.text: Is anything too hard for the LORD? At the set time I will return to you, when the season comes around, and Sarah will have a son.”
promises.context: God responds after Sarah laughed at the promise of a child in old age.

promises.promise: God reassures Abraham that the lasting promise line will be named through Isaac, while also caring for Ishmael.
promises.text: God said to Abraham, “Don’t let it be grievous in your sight because of the boy, and because of your servant. In all that Sarah says to you, listen to her voice. For your offspring will be named through Isaac.
promises.context: When Sarah asked Abraham to send Hagar and Ishmael away after Isaac’s weaning feast.

promises.promise: God hears the boy crying and tells Hagar not to be afraid. He promises to make Ishmael a great nation.
promises.text: God heard the voice of the boy. The angel of God called to Hagar out of the sky, and said to her, “What troubles you, Hagar? Don’t be afraid. For God has heard the voice of the boy where he is. Get up, lift up the boy, and hold him with your hand. For I will make him a great nation.”
promises.context: Hagar and Ishmael were cast out and wandering in the wilderness of Beersheba.

promises.promise: Because Abraham did not withhold Isaac, God swears to multiply his children like stars and sand, give them victory, and bless all nations through his children.
promises.text: that I will bless you greatly, and I will multiply your offspring greatly like the stars of the heavens, and like the sand which is on the seashore. Your offspring will possess the gate of his enemies. All the nations of the earth will be blessed by your offspring, because you have obeyed my voice.’”
promises.context: After Abraham’s obedience on Mount Moriah when God provided a ram.

promises.promise: God will be with Isaac, bless him, give him the lands, multiply his children like the stars, and bless all nations through his children.
promises.text: Live in this land, and I will be with you, and will bless you. For I will give to you, and to your offspring, all these lands, and I will establish the oath which I swore to Abraham your father. I will multiply your offspring as the stars of the sky, and will give all these lands to your offspring. In your offspring all the nations of the earth will be blessed,
promises.context: During a famine, God tells Isaac not to go down to Egypt but to stay in the land.

promises.promise: God tells Isaac not to be afraid. He is with him, will bless him, and will multiply his children for Abraham’s sake.
promises.text: The LORD appeared to him the same night, and said, “I am the God of Abraham your father. Don’t be afraid, for I am with you, and will bless you, and multiply your offspring for my servant Abraham’s sake.”
promises.context: At Beersheba, after conflict over wells with the Philistines.

promises.promise: God promises Jacob the land and countless children, blessing for all families through him, and his own presence—to watch over him, bring him home, and keep every word.
promises.text: Behold, the LORD stood above it, and said, “I am the LORD, the God of Abraham your father, and the God of Isaac. I will give the land you lie on to you and to your offspring. Your offspring will be as the dust of the earth, and you will spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south. In you and in your offspring, all the families of the earth will be blessed. Behold, I am with you, and will keep you, wherever you go, and will bring you again into this land. For I will not leave you until I have done that which I have spoken of to you.”
promises.context: Jacob’s dream of the stairway at Bethel while fleeing from Esau.

promises.promise: God tells Jacob to return home and promises, “I will be with you.”
promises.text: The LORD said to Jacob, “Return to the land of your fathers, and to your relatives, and I will be with you.”
promises.context: After years with Laban, when tension had grown over Jacob’s prosperity.

promises.promise: God gives a new name to Jacob as Israel, promises nations and kings from him, and confirms the land given to Abraham and Isaac.
promises.text: God said to him, “Your name is Jacob. Your name shall not be Jacob any more, but your name will be Israel.” He named him Israel. God said to him, “I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation and a company of nations will be from you, and kings will come out of your body. The land which I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I will give it to you, and to your offspring after you I will give the land.”
promises.context: God appears again to Jacob at Bethel after he returned from Paddan Aram.

promises.promise: God tells Jacob not to be afraid to go to Egypt. He will make him a great nation there, go with him, and bring him home again.
promises.text: He said, “I am God, the God of your father. Don’t be afraid to go down into Egypt, for there I will make of you a great nation. I will go down with you into Egypt. I will also surely bring you up again. Joseph’s hand will close your eyes.”
promises.context: At Beersheba, as Jacob prepared to reunite with Joseph in Egypt during famine.

promises.promise: Jacob trusts God’s promise: God will be with Joseph and bring him back to the land of his fathers.
promises.text: Israel said to Joseph, “Behold, I am dying, but God will be with you, and bring you again to the land of your fathers.
promises.context: Jacob blesses Joseph’s sons Ephraim and Manasseh near the end of his life.

promises.promise: Joseph trusts God’s promise: God will surely visit his people and bring them up to the land promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
promises.text: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am dying, but God will surely visit you, and bring you up out of this land to the land which he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.”
promises.context: Joseph’s dying words in Egypt, looking forward to the exodus.

promises.promise: God promises that he has surely seen his people’s affliction, heard their cry, and know their sorrows; he has come down to deliver them and bring them to a good and large land.
promises.text: The LORD said, “I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and have heard their cry because of their taskmasters, for I know their sorrows. I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land to a good and large land, to a land flowing with milk and honey; to the place of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.

promises.promise: God promises Moses, “I will certainly be with you.” His presence is the sign that God has sent him.
promises.text: He said, “Certainly I will be with you. This will be the token to you, that I have sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God on this mountain.”

promises.promise: God tells Moses his name: “I AM WHO I AM.” He is the living God who sends help to his people.
promises.text: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM,” and he said, “You shall tell the children of Israel this: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”

promises.promise: God tells Moses to go, and promises to be with his mouth and teach him what to say.
promises.text: Now therefore go, and I will be with your mouth, and teach you what you shall speak.”

promises.promise: God promises to free his people from slavery, take them as his own, and bring them into the land he swore to give them. He will be their God.
promises.text: God spoke to Moses, and said to him, “I am the LORD. I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, as God Almighty; but by my name the LORD I was not known to them. I have also established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their travels, in which they lived as aliens. Moreover I have heard the groaning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians keep in bondage, and I have remembered my covenant. Therefore tell the children of Israel, ‘I am the LORD, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will rid you out of their bondage, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm, and with great judgments. I will take you to myself for a people. I will be your God; and you shall know that I am the LORD your God, who brings you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians. I will bring you into the land which I swore to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will give it to you for a heritage: I am the LORD.’”
promises.context: Lasting promise name and seven I wills.

promises.promise: God promises that when he sees the blood, he will pass over that home. The plague of destruction will not touch them.
promises.text: The blood shall be to you for a token on the houses where you are. When I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague will be on you to destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.

promises.promise: God tells his people not to be afraid. Stand still and see him save you—he will fight for you.
promises.text: Moses said to the people, “Don’t be afraid. Stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD, which he will work for you today; for you will never again see the Egyptians whom you have seen today. The LORD will fight for you, and you shall be still.”

promises.promise: God is your strength and your song. He becomes your salvation—the God you can praise.
promises.text: The LORD is my strength and song. He has become my salvation. This is my God, and I will praise him; my father’s God, and I will exalt him.

promises.promise: You, in your faithful love, have led the people that you have redeemed. You have guided them in your strength to your holy habitation.
promises.text: “You, in your loving kindness, have led the people that you have redeemed. You have guided them in your strength to your holy habitation.

promises.promise: God promises that when his people listen and walk in his ways, he watches over them as the Lord who heals.
promises.text: He said, “If you will diligently listen to the LORD your God’s voice, and will do that which is right in his eyes, and will pay attention to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of the diseases on you which I have put on the Egyptians; for I am the LORD who heals you.”

promises.promise: God promises to rain bread from heaven each day—enough for the day—so his people can learn to trust him.
promises.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I will rain bread from the sky for you, and the people shall go out and gather a day’s portion every day, that I may test them, whether they will walk in my law or not.

promises.promise: God promises that at evening you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with bread; you will know that he is the Lord your God.
promises.text: “I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel. Speak to them, saying, ‘At evening you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall be filled with bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.’”

promises.promise: God reminds Israel he carried them on eagles’ wings to himself. If they listen and keep his promise, they will be his treasured people—a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.
promises.text: ‘You have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I bore you on eagles’ wings, and brought you to myself. Now therefore, if you will indeed obey my voice and keep my covenant, then you shall be my own possession from among all peoples; for all the earth is mine; and you shall be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.’ These are the words which you shall speak to the children of Israel.”

promises.promise: God says he is the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
promises.text: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

promises.promise: God is deeply serious about loyalty—and he shows faithful love to thousands of those who love him and keep his ways.
promises.text: you shall not bow yourself down to them, nor serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, on the third and on the fourth generation of those who hate me, and showing loving kindness to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.

promises.promise: Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land which the Lord your God gives you.
promises.text: “Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land which the LORD your God gives you.

promises.promise: God promises to send an angel ahead to guard the way and bring his people to the place he prepared. When they listen, he stands against their enemies.
promises.text: “Behold, I send an angel before you, to keep you by the way, and to bring you into the place which I have prepared. Pay attention to him, and listen to his voice. Don’t provoke him, for he will not pardon your disobedience, for my name is in him. But if you indeed listen to his voice, and do all that I speak, then I will be an enemy to your enemies, and an adversary to your adversaries.

promises.promise: God promises to care for those who follow him—providing what they need and watching over their lives with his blessing.
promises.text: You shall serve the LORD your God, and he will bless your bread and your water, and I will take sickness away from among you. No one will miscarry or be barren in your land. I will fulfill the number of your days.

promises.promise: God says he will not drive them out in one year; little by little I will drive them out before you, until you have increased and inherit the land.
promises.text: I will not drive them out from before you in one year, lest the land become desolate, and the animals of the field multiply against you. Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you have increased and inherit the land.

promises.promise: God promises to live among his people and be their God. They will know he is the Lord who brought them out of Egypt.
promises.text: I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will be their God. They shall know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, that I might dwell among them: I am the LORD their God.

promises.promise: God promises, “My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.” You are not left to walk alone.
promises.text: He said, “My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”
promises.context: After Israel’s failure with the golden calf.

promises.promise: God tells Moses he will do what he asked—because Moses has found favor, and God knows him by name.
promises.text: The LORD said to Moses, “I will do this thing also that you have spoken; for you have found favor in my sight, and I know you by name.”
promises.context: God knows his servant by name.

promises.promise: God promises to let all his goodness pass before Moses and to show mercy as he chooses. His goodness is real and free.
promises.text: He said, “I will make all my goodness pass before you, and will proclaim the LORD’s name before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy.”
promises.context: God shows his goodness and mercy.

promises.promise: God shows who he is: merciful and gracious, slow to anger, full of faithful love and truth. He forgives sin—and he is also just.
promises.text: The LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed, “The LORD! The LORD, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth, keeping loving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity and disobedience and sin; and who will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, and on the children’s children, on the third and on the fourth generation.”
promises.context: God tells Moses what he is like.

promises.promise: God makes a lasting promise: before his people he will do wonders never seen before on the earth.
promises.text: He said, “Behold, I make a covenant: before all your people I will do marvels, such as have not been worked in all the earth, nor in any nation; and all the people among whom you are shall see the work of the LORD; for it is an awesome thing that I do with you.

promises.promise: God promises that when his people walk in his ways, he gives rain, harvest, and peace. They can lie down without fear.
promises.text: “‘If you walk in my statutes and keep my commandments, and do them, then I will give you your rains in their season, and the land shall yield its increase, and the trees of the field shall yield their fruit. Your threshing shall continue until the vintage, and the vintage shall continue until the sowing time. You shall eat your bread to the full, and dwell in your land safely. “‘I will give peace in the land, and you shall lie down, and no one will make you afraid. I will remove evil animals out of the land, neither shall the sword go through your land.
promises.context: Blessings promised when people walk with God.

promises.promise: God promises to look on his people with favor, make them fruitful, and keep his lasting promise. He will live among them and be their God.
promises.text: “‘I will have respect for you, make you fruitful, multiply you, and will establish my covenant with you. You shall eat old supplies long kept, and you shall move out the old because of the new. I will set my tent among you, and my soul won’t abhor you. I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you will be my people.
promises.context: God promises to be close to his people.

promises.promise: God reminds his people: he brought them out of Egypt so they would not be slaves. He broke their yoke and made them walk upright.
promises.text: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that you should not be their slaves. I have broken the bars of your yoke, and made you walk upright.
promises.context: God frees his people from slavery.

promises.promise: If people confess their sin and humble their hearts, God promises to remember his lasting promise with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—and remember the land.
promises.text: “‘If they confess their iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers, in their trespass which they trespassed against me; and also that because they walked contrary to me, I also walked contrary to them, and brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised heart is humbled, and they then accept the punishment of their iniquity, then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham; and I will remember the land.
promises.context: When people turn back, God remembers his promise.

promises.promise: Even in an enemy’s land, God will not reject his people to destroy them or break his lasting promise. He is still the Lord who remembers.
promises.text: Yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly and to break my covenant with them; for I am the LORD their God. But I will for their sake remember the covenant of their ancestors, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, that I might be their God. I am the LORD.’”
promises.context: Even in hard places, God will not abandon his promise.

promises.promise: God promises his blessing over you: he will keep you, look on you with kindness, and give you peace.
promises.text: ‘The LORD bless you, and keep you. The LORD make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. The LORD lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’
promises.context: The priestly blessing God gave for his people.

promises.promise: The ark went before them to seek out a resting place; the cloud of the Lord was over them by day when they set forward.
promises.text: They set forward from the Mount of the LORD three days’ journey. The ark of the LORD’s covenant went before them three days’ journey, to seek out a resting place for them. The cloud of the LORD was over them by day, when they set forward from the camp.
promises.context: God leads his people toward rest.

promises.promise: Let the Lord’s power be great as you spoken: the Lord is slow to anger, abundant in faithful love, forgiving sin—pardon please according to your great faithful love.
promises.text: Now please let the power of the Lord be great, according as you have spoken, saying, ‘The LORD is slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, forgiving iniquity and disobedience; and he will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, on the third and on the fourth generation.’ Please pardon the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of your loving kindness, and just as you have forgiven this people, from Egypt even until now.”

promises.promise: God says he has pardoned as Moses asked. And as surely as he lives, the whole earth will be filled with his glory.
promises.text: The LORD said, “I have pardoned according to your word; but in very deed—as I live, and as all the earth shall be filled with the LORD’s glory—
promises.context: God forgives in answer to prayer.

promises.promise: God promises that remember and do my commandments and be holy to your God. he is the Lord your God who brought you out of Egypt to be your God.
promises.text: so that you may remember and do all my commandments, and be holy to your God. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God: I am the LORD your God.”

promises.promise: God provides a way to live: anyone bitten who looks at the bronze serpent on the pole will live.
promises.text: The LORD said to Moses, “Make a venomous snake, and set it on a pole. It shall happen that everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, shall live.” Moses made a serpent of bronze, and set it on the pole. If a serpent had bitten any man, when he looked at the serpent of bronze, he lived.
promises.context: God provides a way to live—later pointed to by Jesus.

promises.promise: God is not like people who break their word. What he has said, he will do. You can trust his promise.
promises.text: God is not a man, that he should lie, nor a son of man, that he should repent. Has he said, and he won’t do it? Or has he spoken, and he won’t make it good? Behold, I have received a command to bless. He has blessed, and I can’t reverse it.
promises.context: Even Balaam must say God keeps his word.

promises.promise: He has not seen sin in Jacob; the Lord his God is with him. The shout of a king is among them.
promises.text: He has not seen iniquity in Jacob. Neither has he seen perverseness in Israel. The LORD his God is with him. The shout of a king is among them.
promises.context: God is with his people as their King.

promises.promise: God paints a picture of blessing for Israel—good tents, flowing water, and a rising kingdom under his care.
promises.text: How goodly are your tents, Jacob, and your dwellings, Israel! As valleys they are spread out, as gardens by the riverside, as aloes which the LORD has planted, as cedar trees beside the waters. Water shall flow from his buckets. His seed shall be in many waters. His king shall be higher than Agag. His kingdom shall be exalted.
promises.context: A vision of blessing for God’s people.

promises.promise: God promises a coming ruler: a star out of Jacob, a scepter rising out of Israel—not yet, but surely.
promises.text: I see him, but not now. I see him, but not near. A star will come out of Jacob. A scepter will rise out of Israel, and shall strike through the corners of Moab, and crush all the sons of Sheth.
promises.context: A promise of a coming ruler.

promises.promise: Do not be terrified. God goes before you and will fight for you—just as he did in Egypt and in the wilderness, carrying you like a father carries his child.
promises.text: Then I said to you, “Don’t be terrified. Don’t be afraid of them. The LORD your God, who goes before you, he will fight for you, according to all that he did for you in Egypt before your eyes, and in the wilderness where you have seen how that the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, in all the way that you went, until you came to this place.”
promises.context: Moses reminds the people how God fought for them.

promises.promise: These forty years the Lord your God has been with you; you have lacked nothing.
promises.text: For the LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He has known your walking through this great wilderness. These forty years, the LORD your God has been with you. You have lacked nothing.
promises.context: Looking back on God’s care in the wilderness.

promises.promise: What great nation is there that has a god so near to them as the Lord our God is whenever we call on him?
promises.text: For what great nation is there that has a god so near to them as the LORD our God is whenever we call on him?
promises.context: God is near when his people call.

promises.promise: If you seek God with all your heart and soul, you will find him. He is merciful—he will not fail you, destroy you, or forget his lasting promise.
promises.text: But from there you shall seek the LORD your God, and you will find him when you search after him with all your heart and with all your soul. When you are in oppression, and all these things have come on you, in the latter days you shall return to the LORD your God and listen to his voice. For the LORD your God is a merciful God. He will not fail you nor destroy you, nor forget the covenant of your fathers which he swore to them.
promises.context: Hope for people far from home.

promises.promise: Know today that the Lord is God in heaven above and on earth beneath; there is no other. Keep his ways that it may go well with you and your children, and you may prolong days in the land.
promises.text: Know therefore today, and take it to heart, that the LORD himself is God in heaven above and on the earth beneath. There is no one else. You shall keep his statutes and his commandments which I command you today, that it may go well with you and with your children after you, and that you may prolong your days in the land which the LORD your God gives you for all time.

promises.promise: Faithful love to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.
promises.text: You shall not bow yourself down to them, nor serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children and on the third and on the fourth generation of those who hate me and showing loving kindness to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.
promises.context: In the Ten Commandments, God also speaks of mercy.

promises.promise: God longs for his people’s good—that they would have hearts to honor him, so it may go well with them and their children forever.
promises.text: Oh that there were such a heart in them that they would fear me and keep all my commandments always, that it might be well with them and with their children forever!
promises.context: God longs for his people’s good.

promises.promise: Hear, Israel: the Lord is our God; the Lord is one. Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.
promises.text: Hear, Israel: The LORD is our God. The LORD is one. You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.
promises.context: Israel’s core call to love the one true God.

promises.promise: You are a holy people; the Lord has chosen you to be a people for his own possession—not because you were many, but because the Lord loves you and keeps the oath he swore to your fathers.
promises.text: For you are a holy people to the LORD your God. The LORD your God has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth. The LORD didn’t set his love on you nor choose you, because you were more in number than any people; for you were the fewest of all peoples; but because the LORD loves you, and because he desires to keep the oath which he swore to your fathers, the LORD has brought you out with a mighty hand and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
promises.context: God chose his people because he loves them.

promises.promise: Know that the Lord your God is God—the faithful God who keeps his lasting promise and faithful love for a thousand generations of those who love him.
promises.text: Know therefore that the LORD your God himself is God, the faithful God, who keeps covenant and loving kindness to a thousand generations with those who love him and keep his commandments,
promises.context: God is faithful to keep his promises.

promises.promise: If you listen to instructions, the Lord will keep lasting promise faithful love; he will love you, bless you, multiply you—bless fruit of body, ground, and cattle in the land he swore.
promises.text: It shall happen, because you listen to these ordinances and keep and do them, that the LORD your God will keep with you the covenant and the loving kindness which he swore to your fathers. He will love you, bless you, and multiply you. He will also bless the fruit of your body and the fruit of your ground, your grain and your new wine and your oil, the increase of your livestock and the young of your flock, in the land which he swore to your fathers to give you.
promises.context: Blessings that flow from walking with God.

promises.promise: the Lord will take away from you all sickness; he will put none of the evil diseases of Egypt on you.
promises.text: The LORD will take away from you all sickness; and he will put none of the evil diseases of Egypt, which you know, on you, but will lay them on all those who hate you.
promises.context: God’s care for his people’s well-being.

promises.promise: Remember how God led you in the wilderness. He fed you with manna; your clothes did not wear out, and your feet did not swell for forty years.
promises.text: You shall remember all the way which the LORD your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, that he might humble you, to test you, to know what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments or not. He humbled you, allowed you to be hungry, and fed you with manna, which you didn’t know, neither did your fathers know, that he might teach you that man does not live by bread only, but man lives by every word that proceeds out of the LORD’s mouth. Your clothing didn’t grow old on you, neither did your foot swell, these forty years.
promises.context: A reminder of how God cared in hard places.

promises.promise: the Lord brings you into a good land—brooks, springs, wheat, barley, vines, figs, pomegranates, oil, honey—a land without scarcity; you will eat and be full and bless the Lord.
promises.text: For the LORD your God brings you into a good land, a land of brooks of water, of springs, and underground water flowing into valleys and hills; a land of wheat, barley, vines, fig trees, and pomegranates; a land of olive trees and honey; a land in which you shall eat bread without scarcity, you shall not lack anything in it; a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills you may dig copper. You shall eat and be full, and you shall bless the LORD your God for the good land which he has given you.
promises.context: God brings his people into a good land.

promises.promise: God led you through a hard wilderness—yet he brought water from the rock and fed you with manna, so that he might do you good in the end.
promises.text: who led you through the great and terrible wilderness, with venomous snakes and scorpions, and thirsty ground where there was no water; who poured water for you out of the rock of flint; who fed you in the wilderness with manna, which your fathers didn’t know, that he might humble you, and that he might prove you, to do you good at your latter end;
promises.context: God’s hard path was meant for their good in the end.

promises.promise: Know today that the Lord your God is he who goes over before you as a devouring fire; he will destroy them and bring them down before you.
promises.text: Know therefore today that the LORD your God is he who goes over before you as a devouring fire. He will destroy them and he will bring them down before you. So you shall drive them out and make them perish quickly, as the LORD has spoken to you.
promises.context: God goes ahead of his people.

promises.promise: What does the Lord require but to fear him, walk in his ways, love him, serve with all heart and soul, and keep commandments for your good?
promises.text: Now, Israel, what does the LORD your God require of you, but to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to love him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, to keep the LORD’s commandments and statutes, which I command you today for your good?
promises.context: What God asks is for his people’s good.

promises.promise: the Lord your God is God of gods, who doesn’t regard persons nor take bribes; he executes justice for orphan and widow and loves the foreigner—love the foreigner therefore.
promises.text: For the LORD your God, he is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great God, the mighty, and the awesome, who doesn’t respect persons or take bribes. He executes justice for the fatherless and widow and loves the foreigner in giving him food and clothing. Therefore love the foreigner, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
promises.context: God loves justice and cares for outsiders.

promises.promise: The land drinks water from the rain of heaven; a land the Lord cares for—the eyes of the Lord are always on it, from the beginning of the year to the end.
promises.text: but the land that you go over to possess is a land of hills and valleys which drinks water from the rain of the sky, a land which the LORD your God cares for. The LORD your God’s eyes are always on it, from the beginning of the year even to the end of the year.
promises.context: God watches over the land with care.

promises.promise: Lay up these words in heart and soul. Bind them. Teach children—that your days and your children’s days may be multiplied in the land as the days of the heavens above the earth.
promises.text: Therefore you shall lay up these words of mine in your heart and in your soul. You shall bind them for a sign on your hand, and they shall be for frontlets between your eyes. You shall teach them to your children, talking of them when you sit in your house, when you walk by the way, when you lie down, and when you rise up. You shall write them on the door posts of your house and on your gates; that your days and your children’s days may be multiplied in the land which the LORD swore to your fathers to give them, as the days of the heavens above the earth.
promises.context: Keeping God’s words close brings lasting life.

promises.promise: God promises that he sets before you today a blessing and a curse: blessing if you obey, curse if you don’t.
promises.text: Behold, I set before you today a blessing and a curse: the blessing, if you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God, which I command you today; and the curse, if you do not listen to the commandments of the LORD your God, but turn away out of the way which I command you today, to go after other gods which you have not known.
promises.context: God sets a clear choice before his people.

promises.promise: You have not yet come into the rest God has for you. When you cross the Jordan, he will give you rest from enemies and a safe home.
promises.text: for you haven’t yet come to the rest and to the inheritance which the LORD your God gives you. But when you go over the Jordan and dwell in the land which the LORD your God causes you to inherit, and he gives you rest from all your enemies around you, so that you dwell in safety,

promises.promise: There should be no poor among you—for the Lord will surely bless you in the land—if only you listen; you will lend to many nations and not borrow.
promises.text: However there will be no poor with you (for the LORD will surely bless you in the land which the LORD your God gives you for an inheritance to possess) if only you diligently listen to the LORD your God’s voice, to observe to do all this commandment which I command you today. For the LORD your God will bless you, as he promised you. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow. You will rule over many nations, but they will not rule over you.
promises.context: God’s blessing frees his people to be generous.

promises.promise: God promises that the Lord will raise up a prophet from among you like me; him you shall listen to. he will put my words in his mouth.
promises.text: The LORD your God will raise up to you a prophet from among you, of your brothers, like me. You shall listen to him. This is according to all that you desired of the LORD your God in Horeb in the day of the assembly, saying, “Let me not hear again the LORD my God’s voice, neither let me see this great fire any more, that I not die.” The LORD said to me, “They have well said that which they have spoken. I will raise them up a prophet from among their brothers, like you. I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I shall command him.
promises.context: God promises to raise up a prophet like Moses.

promises.promise: When you face a bigger army, do not be afraid. God is with you. He goes with you to fight for you and to save you.
promises.text: When you go out to battle against your enemies, and see horses, chariots, and a people more numerous than you, you shall not be afraid of them; for the LORD your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt, is with you. It shall be, when you draw near to the battle, that the priest shall approach and speak to the people, and shall tell them, “Hear, Israel, you draw near today to battle against your enemies. Don’t let your heart faint! Don’t be afraid, nor tremble, neither be scared of them; for the LORD your God is he who goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.”
promises.context: God is with his people even in battle.

promises.promise: Nevertheless the Lord your God wouldn’t listen to Balaam, but turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the Lord your God loved you.
promises.text: Nevertheless the LORD your God wouldn’t listen to Balaam, but the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing to you, because the LORD your God loved you.
promises.context: God turns a curse into a blessing because he loves.

promises.promise: the Lord your God walks in the middle of your camp to deliver you; therefore your camp shall be holy.
promises.text: for the LORD your God walks in the middle of your camp, to deliver you, and to give up your enemies before you. Therefore your camp shall be holy, that he may not see an unclean thing in you, and turn away from you.
promises.context: God is present among his people to save them.

promises.promise: You have declared the Lord to be your God; the Lord has declared you to be a people for his own possession—to make you high above all nations for praise, name, and honor, a holy people.
promises.text: You have declared today that the LORD is your God, and that you would walk in his ways, keep his statutes, his commandments, and his ordinances, and listen to his voice. The LORD has declared today that you are a people for his own possession, as he has promised you, and that you should keep all his commandments. He will make you high above all nations that he has made, in praise, in name, and in honor, and that you may be a holy people to the LORD your God, as he has spoken.

promises.promise: If you listen diligently, the Lord will set you high above all nations; blessed in city and field, fruit of body and ground, basket and kneading trough, when you come in and go out.
promises.text: It shall happen, if you shall listen diligently to the LORD your God’s voice, to observe to do all his commandments which I command you today, that the LORD your God will set you high above all the nations of the earth. All these blessings will come upon you, and overtake you, if you listen to the LORD your God’s voice. You shall be blessed in the city, and you shall be blessed in the field. You shall be blessed in the fruit of your body, the fruit of your ground, the fruit of your animals, the increase of your livestock, and the young of your flock. Your basket and your kneading trough shall be blessed. You shall be blessed when you come in, and you shall be blessed when you go out.

promises.promise: the Lord will cause enemies to be struck before you; he will command the blessing on you in your barns and all you put your hand to in the land.
promises.text: The LORD will cause your enemies who rise up against you to be struck before you. They will come out against you one way, and will flee before you seven ways. The LORD will command the blessing on you in your barns, and in all that you put your hand to. He will bless you in the land which the LORD your God gives you.

promises.promise: the Lord will grant abundant prosperity; he will open his good treasury the sky to give rain and bless all the work of your hand; you will lend to many nations.
promises.text: The LORD will grant you abundant prosperity in the fruit of your body, in the fruit of your livestock, and in the fruit of your ground, in the land which the LORD swore to your fathers to give you. The LORD will open to you his good treasure in the sky, to give the rain of your land in its season, and to bless all the work of your hand. You will lend to many nations, and you will not borrow.

promises.promise: When blessings and curses come and you call them to mind among the nations and return to the Lord, he will reverse your captivity and have compassion and gather you from all peoples.
promises.text: It shall happen, when all these things have come on you, the blessing and the curse, which I have set before you, and you shall call them to mind among all the nations where the LORD your God has driven you, and return to the LORD your God and obey his voice according to all that I command you today, you and your children, with all your heart and with all your soul, that then the LORD your God will release you from captivity, have compassion on you, and will return and gather you from all the peoples where the LORD your God has scattered you.

promises.promise: If your outcasts are in the uttermost parts of the heavens, from there the Lord will gather you; he will bring you into the land; he will circumcise your heart and your children’s heart to love him—that you may live.
promises.text: If your outcasts are in the uttermost parts of the heavens, from there the LORD your God will gather you, and from there he will bring you back. The LORD your God will bring you into the land which your fathers possessed, and you will possess it. He will do you good, and increase your numbers more than your fathers. The LORD your God will circumcise your heart, and the heart of your offspring, to love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, that you may live.

promises.promise: You will return and obey; the Lord will make you have abundance in all the work of your hand, fruit of body and cattle and ground—for the Lord will again rejoice over you for good if you turn.
promises.text: You shall return and obey the LORD’s voice, and do all his commandments which I command you today. The LORD your God will make you prosperous in all the work of your hand, in the fruit of your body, in the fruit of your livestock, and in the fruit of your ground, for good; for the LORD will again rejoice over you for good, as he rejoiced over your fathers, if you will obey the LORD your God’s voice, to keep his commandments and his statutes which are written in this book of the law, if you turn to the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.

promises.promise: God’s command is not too hard or far away. His word is very near you—in your mouth and in your heart—so you can do it.
promises.text: For this commandment which I command you today is not too hard for you or too distant. It is not in heaven, that you should say, “Who will go up for us to heaven, bring it to us, and proclaim it to us, that we may do it?” Neither is it beyond the sea, that you should say, “Who will go over the sea for us, bring it to us, and proclaim it to us, that we may do it?” But the word is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, that you may do it.

promises.promise: God promises that he has set before you life and good, death and evil; love the Lord, walk in his ways, keep commandments—that you may live and multiply, and the Lord bless you in the land.
promises.text: Behold, I have set before you today life and prosperity, and death and evil. For I command you today to love the LORD your God, to walk in his ways and to keep his commandments, his statutes, and his ordinances, that you may live and multiply, and that the LORD your God may bless you in the land where you go in to possess it.

promises.promise: God promises that i call heaven and earth to witness: he has set before you life and death, blessing and curse; choose life that you may live—loving the Lord, obeying, clinging—for he is your life and length of days.
promises.text: I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. Therefore choose life, that you may live, you and your descendants, to love the LORD your God, to obey his voice, and to cling to him; for he is your life, and the length of your days, that you may dwell in the land which the LORD swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.

promises.promise: Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid—God goes with you. He will not fail you or leave you.
promises.text: Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or scared of them, for the LORD your God himself is who goes with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you.”

promises.promise: God himself goes before you. He will be with you. He will not fail you or leave you.
promises.text: The LORD himself is who goes before you. He will be with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be discouraged.”
promises.context: God goes ahead of his people.

promises.promise: God's portion is his people; he found him in a desert land, encircled him, cared for him, kept him as the apple of his eye.
promises.text: For the LORD’s portion is his people. Jacob is the lot of his inheritance. He found him in a desert land, in the waste howling wilderness. He surrounded him. He cared for him. He kept him as the apple of his eye.

promises.promise: As an eagle stirs up her nest and flutters over her young, the Lord alone led him; there was no foreign god with him.
promises.text: As an eagle that stirs up her nest, that flutters over her young, he spread abroad his wings, he took them, he bore them on his feathers. The LORD alone led him. There was no foreign god with him.

promises.promise: God will judge his people and have compassion on his servants when he sees their strength is gone.
promises.text: For the LORD will judge his people, and have compassion on his servants, when he sees that their power is gone, that there is no one remaining, shut up or left at large.

promises.promise: God alone is God. He is the one who wounds and heals, who puts to death and makes alive. No one can deliver from his hand.
promises.text: “See now that I myself am he. There is no god with me. I kill and I make alive. I wound and I heal. There is no one who can deliver out of my hand.

promises.promise: The beloved of the Lord will live in safety beside him. God covers him all day long and carries him close.
promises.text: About Benjamin he said, “The beloved of the LORD will dwell in safety by him. He covers him all day long. He dwells between his shoulders.”

promises.promise: There is no one like God, who comes to help you. The eternal God is your home, and underneath you are his everlasting arms.
promises.text: “There is no one like God, Jeshurun, who rides on the heavens for your help, in his excellency on the skies. The eternal God is your dwelling place. Underneath are the everlasting arms. He thrust out the enemy from before you, and said, ‘Destroy!’

promises.promise: Happy are you, Israel. Who is like you, a people saved by the Lord, the shield of your help, the sword of your excellency!
promises.text: You are happy, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD, the shield of your help, the sword of your excellency? Your enemies will submit themselves to you. You will tread on their high places.”

promises.promise: God promises every place Joshua’s foot treads. No one will be able to stand against him. As God was with Moses, so he will be with Joshua—he will not fail or leave him.
promises.text: I have given you every place that the sole of your foot will tread on, as I told Moses. From the wilderness and this Lebanon even to the great river, the river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and to the great sea toward the going down of the sun, shall be your border. No man will be able to stand before you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not fail you nor forsake you.

promises.promise: Be strong and courageous. You will lead this people to inherit the land. Stay strong by carefully keeping God’s ways.
promises.text: “Be strong and courageous; for you shall cause this people to inherit the land which I swore to their fathers to give them. Only be strong and very courageous. Be careful to observe to do according to all the law which Moses my servant commanded you. Don’t turn from it to the right hand or to the left, that you may have good success wherever you go.

promises.promise: God tells Joshua to be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid—the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.
promises.text: This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success. Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.”

promises.promise: God promises that today he will begin to magnify you in the sight of all Israel, that they may know that as I was with Moses, so he will be with you.
promises.text: The LORD said to Joshua, “Today I will begin to magnify you in the sight of all Israel, that they may know that as I was with Moses, so I will be with you.

promises.promise: God promises that see, he has given Jericho into your hand, with its king and mighty men of valor.
promises.text: The LORD said to Joshua, “Behold, I have given Jericho into your hand, with its king and the mighty men of valor.

promises.promise: God promises that don’t fear them, for he has delivered them into your hands. Not a man of them will stand before you.
promises.text: The LORD said to Joshua, “Don’t fear them, for I have delivered them into your hands. Not a man of them will stand before you.”

promises.promise: Moses swore: Surely the land your foot has trodden will be an inheritance to you and children forever, because you followed the Lord fully.
promises.text: Moses swore on that day, saying, ‘Surely the land where you walked shall be an inheritance to you and to your children forever, because you have wholly followed the LORD my God.’

promises.promise: the Lord gave Israel all the land he swore; he gave rest all around; not a man stood; not one word failed of all God's good promises—all came to pass.
promises.text: So the LORD gave to Israel all the land which he swore to give to their fathers. They possessed it, and lived in it. The LORD gave them rest all around, according to all that he swore to their fathers. Not a man of all their enemies stood before them. The LORD delivered all their enemies into their hand. Nothing failed of any good thing which the LORD had spoken to the house of Israel. All came to pass.

promises.promise: One man of you shall chase a thousand; for the Lord your God is he who fights for you as he spoke. Take diligent heed to love the Lord your God.
promises.text: One man of you shall chase a thousand; for it is the LORD your God who fights for you, as he spoke to you. Take good heed therefore to yourselves, that you love the LORD your God.

promises.promise: Not one thing has failed of all the good things the Lord your God spoke; all have come to pass, and not one thing has failed.
promises.text: “Behold, today I am going the way of all the earth. You know in all your hearts and in all your souls that not one thing has failed of all the good things which the LORD your God spoke concerning you. All have happened to you. Not one thing has failed of it.

promises.promise: My heart exults in the Lord; my strength is exalted; there is none holy like the Lord; neither is there any rock like our God.
promises.text: Hannah prayed, and said, “My heart exults in the LORD! My horn is exalted in the LORD. My mouth is enlarged over my enemies, because I rejoice in your salvation. There is no one as holy as the LORD, for there is no one besides you, nor is there any rock like our God.

promises.promise: the Lord kills and makes alive; he brings down to Sheol and brings up; he raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy to sit with princes.
promises.text: “The LORD kills and makes alive. He brings down to Sheol and brings up. The LORD makes poor and makes rich. He brings low, he also lifts up. He raises up the poor out of the dust. He lifts up the needy from the dunghill to make them sit with princes and inherit the throne of glory. For the pillars of the earth are the LORD’s. He has set the world on them.

promises.promise: He will keep the feet of his holy ones; the Lord will judge the ends of the earth; he will give strength to his king and exalt the horn of his chosen one.
promises.text: He will keep the feet of his holy ones, but the wicked will be put to silence in darkness; for no man will prevail by strength. Those who strive with the LORD shall be broken to pieces. He will thunder against them in the sky. “The LORD will judge the ends of the earth. He will give strength to his king, and exalt the horn of his anointed.”

promises.promise: Samuel set up Ebenezer, saying, the Lord helped us until now.
promises.text: Then Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, saying, “The LORD helped us until now.”

promises.promise: the Lord will not forsake his people for his great name’s sake, because it has pleased the Lord to make you a people for himself.
promises.text: For the LORD will not forsake his people for his great name’s sake, because it has pleased the LORD to make you a people for himself.

promises.promise: the Lord doesn’t see as man sees; man looks at outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart.
promises.text: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Don’t look on his face, or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him; for I don’t see as man sees. For man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.”

promises.promise: God promises that i took you from the sheepfold to be prince; he has been with you; he will appoint a place for his people Israel and plant them; he will give you rest from enemies; the Lord will make you a house.
promises.text: Now therefore tell my servant David this: ‘The LORD of Armies says, “I took you from the sheep pen, from following the sheep, to be prince over my people, over Israel. I have been with you wherever you went, and have cut off all your enemies from before you. I will make you a great name, like the name of the great ones who are on the earth. I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in their own place and be moved no more. The children of wickedness will not afflict them any more, as at the first, and as from the day that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel. I will cause you to rest from all your enemies. Moreover the LORD tells you that the LORD will make you a house.

promises.promise: God promises that when your days are fulfilled, he will set up your seed after you; he will build a house for his name, and he will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
promises.text: When your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, I will set up your offspring after you, who will proceed out of your body, and I will establish his kingdom. He will build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.

promises.promise: God says he will be his father, and he will be my son; my faithful love will not depart; your house and kingdom will be made sure forever; your throne established forever.
promises.text: I will be his father, and he will be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men and with the stripes of the children of men; but my loving kindness will not depart from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I put away before you. Your house and your kingdom will be made sure forever before you. Your throne will be established forever.”’”

promises.promise: God promises to be your safe place. When you call on him, he is like a strong rock and shield who protects and rescues you.
promises.text: and he said: “The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer, even mine; God is my rock in whom I take refuge; my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower, and my refuge. My savior, you save me from violence. I call on the LORD, who is worthy to be praised; So shall I be saved from my enemies.

promises.promise: You are my lamp, Lord; the Lord will light up my darkness. God’s way is perfect; his word is tested; he is a shield to all who take refuge.
promises.text: For you are my lamp, LORD. The LORD will light up my darkness. For by you, I run against a troop. By my God, I leap over a wall. As for God, his way is perfect. The LORD’s word is tested. He is a shield to all those who take refuge in him.

promises.promise: God is your strong fortress. He makes your way sure, gives you steady feet, and sets you on high places.
promises.text: God is my strong fortress. He makes my way perfect. He makes his feet like hinds’ feet, and sets me on my high places.

promises.promise: God promises that he has given you a wise and understanding heart; he has also given you what you didn’t ask—riches and honor. If you walk in his ways, he will lengthen your days.
promises.text: behold, I have done according to your word. Behold, I have given you a wise and understanding heart, so that there has been no one like you before you, and after you none will arise like you. I have also given you that which you have not asked, both riches and honor, so that there will not be any among the kings like you for all your days. If you will walk in my ways, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as your father David walked, then I will lengthen your days.”

promises.promise: God promises that if you walk in his ways, he will establish my word with you which I spoke to David; he will dwell among the children of Israel and will not forsake his people.
promises.text: “Concerning this house which you are building, if you will walk in my statutes, and execute my ordinances, and keep all my commandments to walk in them, then I will establish my word with you, which I spoke to David your father. I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will not forsake my people Israel.”

promises.promise: Blessed be the Lord who has given rest to his people Israel according to all he promised; not one word has failed of all his good promise.
promises.text: “Blessed be the LORD, who has given rest to his people Israel, according to all that he promised. There has not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by Moses his servant.

promises.promise: God promises that he has heard your prayer; he has made this house holy; my eyes and my heart shall be there perpetually.
promises.text: The LORD said to him, “I have heard your prayer and your supplication that you have made before me. I have made this house holy, which you have built, to put my name there forever; and my eyes and my heart shall be there perpetually.

promises.promise: God’s word to anxious hearts: don’t be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.
promises.text: He answered, “Don’t be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.”

promises.promise: The remnant will take root downward and bear fruit upward; out of Jerusalem a remnant will go out; the zeal of the Lord will do this.
promises.text: The remnant that has escaped of the house of Judah will again take root downward, and bear fruit upward. For out of Jerusalem a remnant will go out, and out of Mount Zion those who shall escape. The LORD’s zeal will perform this.

promises.promise: God promises that he has heard your prayer; he has seen your tears. he will heal you; on the third day you will go up to God's house.
promises.text: “Turn back, and tell Hezekiah the prince of my people, ‘The LORD, the God of David your father, says, “I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. Behold, I will heal you. On the third day, you will go up to the LORD’s house.

promises.promise: Oh give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his faithful love endures forever.
promises.text: Oh give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever.

promises.promise: God says he will raise up your seed; I will establish his kingdom; he will build me a house; I will establish him in my house and kingdom forever; his throne forever.
promises.text: It will happen, when your days are fulfilled that you must go to be with your fathers, that I will set up your offspring after you, who will be of your sons; and I will establish his kingdom. He will build me a house, and I will establish his throne forever. I will be his father, and he will be my son. I will not take my loving kindness away from him, as I took it from him who was before you; but I will settle him in my house and in my kingdom forever. His throne will be established forever.”’”

promises.promise: Be strong and courageous and do it; don’t be afraid nor dismayed, for the Lord God, my God, is with you; he will not fail you nor forsake you until all the work for God's house is finished.
promises.text: David said to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Don’t be afraid, nor be dismayed, for the LORD God, even my God, is with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you, until all the work for the service of the LORD’s house is finished.

promises.promise: Yours, Lord, is the greatness, power, glory, victory, and majesty; both riches and honor come from you; you rule over all; in your hand is power and might.
promises.text: Yours, LORD, is the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory, and the majesty! For all that is in the heavens and on the earth is yours. Yours is the kingdom, LORD, and you are exalted as head above all. Both riches and honor come from you, and you rule over all! In your hand is power and might! It is in your hand to make great, and to give strength to all!

promises.promise: God promises that if his people who are called by his name humble themselves, pray, seek his face, and turn from wicked ways, then he will hear from heaven, forgive their sin, and heal their land.
promises.text: if my people who are called by my name will humble themselves, pray, seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.

promises.promise: God promises that now my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to prayer in this place; he has chosen and made this house holy that his name may be there forever; my eyes and heart there perpetually.
promises.text: Now my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to prayer that is made in this place. For now I have chosen and made this house holy, that my name may be there forever; and my eyes and my heart will be there perpetually.

promises.promise: God promises to be your safe place. When you call on him, he is like a strong rock and shield who protects and rescues you.
promises.text: He went out to meet Asa, and said to him, “Hear me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin! The LORD is with you while you are with him; and if you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you forsake him, he will forsake you.

promises.promise: Be strong, and do not let your hands grow weak—for your work will be rewarded.
promises.text: But you be strong! Don’t let your hands be slack, for your work will be rewarded.”

promises.promise: The eyes of the Lord run back and forth throughout the whole earth to show himself strong on behalf of those whose heart is perfect toward him.
promises.text: For the LORD’s eyes run back and forth throughout the whole earth, to show himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. You have done foolishly in this; for from now on you will have wars.”

promises.promise: God’s word to anxious hearts: don’t be afraid nor dismayed because of this great multitude; the battle is not yours, but God’s. Stand still and see God's salvation. the Lord is with you.
promises.text: and he said, “Listen, all Judah, and you inhabitants of Jerusalem, and you, King Jehoshaphat. The LORD says to you, ‘Don’t be afraid, and don’t be dismayed because of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s. Tomorrow, go down against them. Behold, they are coming up by the ascent of Ziz. You will find them at the end of the valley, before the wilderness of Jeruel. You will not need to fight this battle. Set yourselves, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD with you, O Judah and Jerusalem. Don’t be afraid, nor be dismayed. Go out against them tomorrow, for the LORD is with you.’”

promises.promise: Believe in the Lord your God, so you will be established; believe his prophets, so you will prosper.
promises.text: They rose early in the morning and went out into the wilderness of Tekoa. As they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, “Listen to me, Judah and you inhabitants of Jerusalem! Believe in the LORD your God, so you will be established! Believe his prophets, so you will prosper.”

promises.promise: God’s hand is for good on all who seek him—but his power is against those who forsake him.
promises.text: For I was ashamed to ask of the king a band of soldiers and horsemen to help us against the enemy on the way, because we had spoken to the king, saying, “The hand of our God is on all those who seek him, for good; but his power and his wrath is against all those who forsake him.”

promises.promise: God’s hand was on his people, and he delivered them from enemies and ambushes along the way.
promises.text: Then we departed from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month, to go to Jerusalem. The hand of our God was on us, and he delivered us from the hand of the enemy and the bandits by the way.

promises.promise: God promises that remember the word: If you trespass he will scatter; but if you return and keep commandments, though scattered to the sky, he will gather from there and bring to the place I chose for his name.
promises.text: “Remember, I beg you, the word that you commanded your servant Moses, saying, ‘If you trespass, I will scatter you among the peoples; but if you return to me, and keep my commandments and do them, though your outcasts were in the uttermost part of the heavens, yet I will gather them from there, and will bring them to the place that I have chosen, to cause my name to dwell there.’

promises.promise: The God of heaven will help us succeed. Therefore his servants will rise and build.
promises.text: Then I answered them, and said to them, “The God of heaven will prosper us. Therefore we, his servants, will arise and build; but you have no portion, nor right, nor memorial in Jerusalem.”

promises.promise: Don’t be grieved, for the joy of the Lord is your strength.
